title: Leaving Armstrong; Tyree Glenn replaces him
summary: Tired of travel, Moore gave notice, and Tyree Glenn took over, clashing with Billy Kyle.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Iceland, we played two or three days there and this time I think I better cut out because this is a little bit too much for me. So I had my notice in to Louie and from there we went to back to New York and we only had a few hours and we have to get warm clothes, "Where we going?" We're going to St. Thomas, Virgin Islands and St. Croix, Virgin Islands. Then from there, we went from Virgin Islands to Puerto Rico, San Juan. And then from Puerto Rico we went to Miami. Then from Miami begin the southern tours and I was getting ready to cut out and Tyree Glenn came all the way from New York to Memphis to hear the band and see what I said, "It's yours, baby." do, you know. / And I told Tyree -- you know, we're pals, we knew each other for years and I told Tyree Glenn that I can't take it, I want to be home with my wife and my family, he said, "Yeh, I'll take over, Chief."

And you know, the story goes now, Billy Kyle rehearses the band, you know, and the background that I do with Louie, Billy Kyle is trying to tell Glenn, Tyree Glenn how to play that and I understand they had a few words together and I don't blame Tyree Glenn, he kind of got peeved at Billy because Billy wanted Tyree to play the same background that I played

behind Louie. And so Tyree told Billy Kyle, 'I'm not Chief, I'm Tyree Glenn, I'll play my own background.' So he did pretty good with the band, you know and after I had left the band they made a movie short of the life of Armstrong that I saw the other night on Channel 13, 'A Portrait of Louie,' or something like that.
So I left Louie finally, they were on their way to Frankfurt, Germany, but I was so glad to be home.
